title: Desktop app from the llama.cpp team (Mac OS and Windows)
content:
Models
Updated Oct 2026
A curated selection of open models — every one runs in llama.app.
Good places to start
LFM 2.5 24B-A2B 24 GB+ memory
Liquid AI's fast local model for reasoning and tool use.
LFM 3 Omni 2B 8 GB+ memory
Liquid AI's tiny omni model for text, images, and audio, from transcribing speech to asking about a photo.
Qwen 3.8 27B 32 GB+ memory
Alibaba's multimodal mid-sized models for coding and research, long-horizon agentic work with 256K native context.
GLM 5.3 320B-A18B 192 GB+ memory
Z.ai's agentic coding model for large setups, with vision and an MTP head for faster generation.
Qwen 3.8 Flash Next 125B-A6B 128 GB+ memory
An experimental preview of the Qwen 4 architecture for long-context agents on large setups, with vision and 256K context.
Muse Glimmer 30B 32 GB+ memory
Meta's local model to run on your laptop powering always-on agents, with coding, tool use, and image understanding.
Gemma 4 E2B E4B 12B 26B-A4B 31B 16 GB+ memory
Google's most capable open agentic models for your laptops, with vision, audio, and support for 140+ languages.
GPT-OSS 20B 120B 24 GB+ memory
OpenAI's open-weight family for local reasoning and agents, with tool use, function calling, and adjustable reasoning effort.
More models
Nemotron 3.5 Super VL 120B-A12B 128 GB+ memory
NVIDIA's large hybrid Mamba-Transformer mixture-of-experts model with vision. Strong at reasoning, coding, and documents, with up to 1M context.
Muse Spark Open 816B-A42B 512 GB+ memory
Meta's large and capable agentic model, takes image and audio input, with adjustable reasoning, and 1M context.
Flint 40B-A2.5B 48 GB+ memory
Recursive's coding-agent model: investigates codebases, fixes bugs, implements features, and writes tests.
Nemotron 3.5 Lightning 30B-A3B 32 GB+ memory
NVIDIA's efficient long-context model for local agents with switchable reasoning mode and up to 1M context.
Laguna XS 2.1 33B-A3B 32 GB+ memory
Poolside's compact coding agent for long-horizon work, with interleaved reasoning and 256K context.
Laguna S 2.1 118B-A8B 96 GB+ memory
Poolside's larger coding model for large software projects with 1M context.
DeepSeek V4 304B 192 GB+ memory
DeepSeek's reasoning and coding model for large setups, combining sparse MoE efficiency with 1M context.
Qwen 3.6 27B 35B-A3B 32 GB+ memory
Alibaba's efficient multimodal models that punch above their size for coding, reasoning, and vision tasks.
GLM 4.7 Flash 32 GB+ memory
Z.ai's fast local agentic coding model, built for software engineering, browser automation, and multi-turn tool use.
Qwen 3.5 Small 0.8B 8 GB+ memory
Alibaba's compact multimodal reasoning models for phones and laptops, with vision, switchable thinking, and support for 201 languages.
Devstral 2 24B 123B 24 GB+ memory
Mistral AI's mid-sized models for autonomous software agents, built to explore repositories, edit across files, and solve engineering tasks.
Ministral 3 3B 3B Reasoning 8B 8B Reasoning 14B 14B Reasoning 8 GB+ memory
Mistral AI's compact multimodal models for on-device apps, offering strong performance across 3B, 8B, and 14B sizes.
Decision models
Models that take a document and typed questions, and return a probability for each option -- route a ticket, moderate content, pick an agent’s next step. They don’t chat; apps call them through the API. How to use ↗
Kev 0.8B 4B 9B 8 GB+ memory
Decision models that take context and typed questions as input, and output a calibrated probability for each option.
Clef Flash 9B 16 GB+ memory
Cloudflare's decision model. Reads a text, JSON, or image state and returns a probability for every option of every typed question in a single pass.
Laya 421M 8 GB+ memory
A multilingual decision model for documents and structured data, returning calibrated probabilities across 100+ languages.
Bespoke Nimble 9B 16 GB+ memory Non-commercial
Bespoke Labs' mid-sized decision model. Given a context and typed questions, it returns a probability for each option.
Embedding models
Models that turn text — and, for some, images and audio — into vectors, for search, retrieval, and clustering. They don’t chat; apps call them through the API. How to use ↗
Find thousands more GGUF models on Hugging Face ↗, then choose Llama under “Use this model” on a model’s page.

report.summary: The llama.cpp team has released a curated desktop model catalog for macOS and Windows, listing open models with the memory each one needs to run locally.
report.background: llama.cpp began as a hobbyist C/C++ port of Meta's LLaMA and grew into the de facto engine for local inference, thanks to its GGUF quantization format and aggressive CPU/GPU optimization. For years, running models locally meant juggling quant levels, context sizes and VRAM math — powerful but unfriendly. Meanwhile, open-weight releases from Alibaba, Google, Meta, Mistral, NVIDIA, OpenAI and others exploded, and unified-memory machines like Apple Silicon made large models feasible on a desk. The missing piece was a consumer-grade front end with a trustworthy answer to 'which model actually fits my machine?' This catalog, paired with a first-party desktop app for macOS and Windows, attempts to answer that with explicit memory tiers — mirroring the broader industry shift toward on-device agents, privacy-preserving inference and per-token cost avoidance.
key_points: Every entry carries an explicit memory floor — from 8 GB for tiny models up to 512 GB for the 816B flagship — turning the usual guesswork about quantization, context and VRAM into a simple lookup table before download.

The lineup is tiered by hardware, not by benchmark: compact 0.8B–14B models for laptops and phones, 24B–35B workhorses for 24–48 GB machines, and 100B+ sparse mixture-of-experts models for 96–512 GB setups.

Local agents and coding dominate the curation: Devstral, Flint, Laguna, GLM Flash and Qwen target repository exploration, multi-file edits, tool calling and browser automation, with 256K to 1M token context windows.

Two non-conversational model classes appear alongside chat models: decision models that return calibrated probabilities for typed questions, and embedding models for search and retrieval — both called through an API rather than a chat window.

The catalog stays open-ecosystem: users can pull thousands more GGUF models from Hugging Face and route them into the app via the 'Use this model' Llama option, so the curated list is a starting point rather than a walled garden.

Multimodality is assumed rather than exceptional — vision, audio transcription and 140+ language support show up from the 2B tier upward, signalling that local models are being positioned as always-on sensing agents.
report.impact: For the AI industry, a first-party app from the llama.cpp team legitimizes local inference as a distribution channel: model labs now have a reason to publish GGUF weights and to optimize for consumer memory tiers rather than datacenter GPUs. Developers get a de facto target spec — if your model runs in llama.app at a stated RAM budget, it runs anywhere — plus standardized decision and embedding endpoints that make classical ML tasks feel like ordinary API calls. Regular users gain privacy, offline operation and no per-token billing, but also a hard hardware gate: the most capable entries demand 128–512 GB of unified memory, reinforcing the divide between well-equipped workstations and ordinary laptops. Expect cloud providers to feel pressure at the low end of the market.
report.tools: Watch llama.cpp itself, the GGUF format and the llama.app desktop client as the reference stack. For alternatives and comparison, try Ollama and LM Studio for one-click local serving, Open WebUI as a chat front end, and Hugging Face's GGUF search to browse beyond the curated list. If you want to build on the decision and embedding models, budget RAM first, then wire the app's local API into your own scripts.
